subject: ICMP path MTU drift — probe and remediation plan
messages:
From: Alexandra King <alexandra@northwood-health.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet failures to private deployment

Hi Jasmine —

We've been seeing intermittent failures when our on‑prem devices talk to the private deployment in us-west-2. Symptoms: long stalls for ~20–40s then retransmits, TCP sessions recover after fragmentation. It looks correlated with ~1500->9000 MTU transitions on our path.

I attached a short pcap taken at our border during one failure (tcpdump-nwh-20270218.pcap). Notably we see lots of "ICMP Destination Unreachable (Fragmentation needed)" but the ICMPs are not reaching the endpoints consistently.

Can Redwood take a look? This impacts a handful of customers hitting our VPN-backed private endpoints. We're happy to run commands if you need more traces.

Thanks,
Alexandra King
Engineering Operations
Northwood Health
Attachment: tcpdump-nwh-20270218.pcap (pcap, 2.3MB)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alexandra@northwood-health.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet failures to private deployment — please triage

Folks — forwarding a report from Northwood. They see fragmentation-needed ICMPs but packets aren't flowing. This is a live production impact affecting their hybrid private deployment (VPC peered via customer-managed VPN).

Quick asks:
- Can infra/network confirm whether our GRE/IPsec endpoints are clamping MTU in the path?
- Check if any firewall/SGs are dropping ICMP type 3/code 4 messages (needed for PMTU).
- If we need a short mitigation, recommend MSS clamp on NAT or adjust GRE MTU.

Alexandra is copied in. Please keep the thread for timeline/audit.

Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alexandra@northwood-health.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet failures to private deployment — please triage

Thanks Jasmine — I pulled the customer's pcap. Quick findings:
- I see ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation needed, DF set) originating from an intermediate device.
- Subsequent ICMP responses appear filtered intermittently; some are dropped by a hop that looks like their upstream firewall.
- There are also packets with DF set sized ~1500 that travel into a region where the next hop expects >1500 (jumbo path). This asymmetric MTU/DF handling is causing PMTU probes to fail and TCP to fall back only after retransmits.

Immediate checks I want the customer to run (Alexandra, if you can provide results here):
- On your border router, run: sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 icmp and "icmp[0] == 3" -w pmtu-icmp.pcap (10s during a repro)
- traceroute -F -w 2 -q 1 <private-endpoint-ip> (this traces with DF set to force PMTU path behavior)
- Show us "ip link" or "ifconfig" for the tunnel endpoints and the tunnel MTU (are they 1500 vs 9000?).

Quick mitigations we can push from our side while we investigate:
- Apply an MSS clamp on the egress NAT for sessions bound for the private endpoints (suggest 1400).
- Confirm GRE tunnel MTU on our edge and drop / adjust to match their path if necessary.
- Ensure security groups and border firewalls allow ICMP type 3 code 4.

I'll draft a short runbook for the MSS clamp and GRE MTU tweak. If customer allows, we can schedule a 10‑minute window to apply a temporary MSS clamp.

Jonas Weber
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alexandra King <alexandra@northwood-health.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet failures to private deployment — please triage

Thanks Jonas — attaching the traceroute/mtu probes we ran (mtu-probe-log.txt). Our edge is configured with jumbo frames (MTU 9000) for internal fabric, but the customer VPN and our on‑prem firewall uses 1500 on the external interface. The GRE tunnel to Redwood's edge is negotiated as 1500 on our side, but I see 9000 on the fabric side which could explain the asymmetry.

We also noticed that our upstream firewall (managed by a third party) suppresses ICMP in some windowed cases — they claim it's to reduce amplification risks. I can try to get them to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 for this destination.

We are OK with a short MSS clamp if Redwood can coordinate and then revert after we confirm.

Alexandra
Attachment: mtu-probe-log.txt (text, 6KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alexandra@northwood-health.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent large-packet failures to private deployment — remediation plan

Plan and immediate actions (summary for audit):
1) Short mitigation (apply within 10min, low-risk):
   - Add egress MSS clamp on our NAT gateway for flows destined to Northwood's prefix: set mss 1400.
   - Command (example): iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -d <northwood-prefix> -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

2) Longer-term fixes (requires coordination):
   - Align MTU across GRE/IPsec endpoints. If Northwood wants to keep 9000 internally, we need to configure GRE MTU on our edge and any transit devices to support jumbo frames end-to-end or ensure encapsulation accounts for overhead.
   - Confirm upstream/third-party firewall policy to allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 for PMTU. Document the acceptance window and verify with test captures.
   - Add proactive PMTU monitoring: periodic traceroutes with DF set and alert if ICMP path failures > threshold.

3) Rollback plan:
   - MSS clamp removal command: iptables -t mangle -D POSTROUTING ... (recorded in runbook).
   - If MSS clamp causes any regressions, revert within 5 minutes and open emergency tracking.

I've attached a small helper script to apply the GRE MTU and MSS clamp on our edge for the on-call run (redwood-gre-mtu-fix.sh). I'll coordinate a 10-minute maintenance window with Alexandra.

Next steps: Jonas and I will schedule the window for today at 16:00 PST unless customer requests otherwise. Alexandra — please confirm upstream firewall can permit ICMP type 3/code 4 during the window.

Rishi Malhotra
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-gre-mtu-fix.sh (script, 4KB)
